definitions.I2: Meaning-equivalent texts may induce different cognitive paths/experiences.
definitions.I3: The proposed accessibility boundary of meaning is not determined by language alone.
definitions.I4: Physical reality is proposed as a constraint on accessible meaning.
definitions.I5: Finite character/symbolic carriers can be used to probe a larger meaning space.
definitions.I6: The same meaning can admit multiple expressions.
definitions.I7: Expression multiplicity can coexist with a boundary on accessible meaning.
definitions.I8: Surface character replacement is distinguished from reaching a new meaning topology.
